title: Names and plural nouns: one verb for all

sections.title: Explanation
sections.content: Whenever the subject is more than one person, the verb takes *-nak/-nek*, whether you say *ők*, two names or a plural noun. *Anna és Károly olvasnak.* *A gyerekek tanulnak.* With one person the verb stays plain: *A gyerek tanul.*

items.spanish: Anna és Károly a konyhában főznek.
items.english: Anna and Károly cook in the kitchen.
The children walk in the garden.
Meg and Mariann do not write.

sections.content: Do not add *-nak* to a single person: *A barát ír.* is one friend writing, *A barátok írnak.* is several.
